title: Issue #128: Architecture: decentralized Crypto Service for users and developers
content:
State: open

Timestamp: 2026-10-15 00:28 CEST
Version: 0.1.0
Watermark: A-TownChain / Globus OS — Architecture Proposal

# Objective

Specify a decentralized Crypto Service for A-TownChain serving both end users and developers from the outset. This issue is an architecture and contract task; it does not claim that any listed service is implemented, secure, or production-ready.

Guiding principle: **Standalone First, Ecosystem Second.** Preserve canonical implementation ownership and do not create duplicate wallet, blockchain-core, VM, consensus, or standards implementations in the ecosystem repository.

# User-facing services

- Wallet: open-source web/mobile client, address and asset display, transaction construction, local signing, fee estimation, address book, backup/recovery UX, phishing warnings, and explicit approval for privileged actions.
- Payments: versioned merchant/payment request contract, invoice/reference metadata, confirmations/finality status, refunds and idempotent payment handling where supported.
- Explorer: blocks, transactions, accounts, assets and contract activity, with clear confirmation/finality labels and source provenance. An indexer/explorer is a derived view, never canonical state.
- Token/NFT/marketplace and DeFi interfaces: only after canonical asset/contract standards, deterministic execution, audits, and economic/security constraints are defined.
- Governance interface: proposal and voting UX only where a normative governance protocol exists.
- Fiat on/off ramps: optional third-party integrations; require provider, jurisdiction, compliance, custody and availability disclosures. They are not protocol dependencies.

# Developer and enterprise services

- Community-operated RPC endpoints and optional REST/WebSocket adapters; document rate limits, authentication, endpoint provenance, service-level metrics and abuse controls.
- Versioned SDKs and API contracts, initially prioritizing the languages supported by canonical repositories and standards.
- Explorer/indexer APIs and event subscriptions, with reorg/finality handling and deterministic cursor/pagination semantics.
- Smart-contract tooling and templates only for the canonical ATC-VM/ATCLang and their normative interfaces; no second VM, bytecode format or contract standard.
- Testnet/devnet tooling, local-node setup, conformance fixtures, examples and reproducible integration tests.
- Optional storage and oracle adapters. External services must be explicitly identified, versioned and treated according to declared trust assumptions.

# Decentralization and trust model

- Publish clients, contracts, protocol schemas and service-node software under the project’s approved open-source policies.
- Permit independent operators to run nodes and services; users/developers must be able to choose and change providers without a single mandatory gateway.
- Avoid a mandatory central RPC, hosted indexer, identity provider, wallet backend or frontend.
- Provide multiple independently operated discovery/bootstrap sources and document residual coordination dependencies.
- Keep private keys and signing authority client-side by default. Any custodial, MPC, recovery or social-login design requires a separate threat model and explicit opt-in.
- Service rewards, fees, staking, slashing and token issuance must not be invented in this issue. Any incentive model requires a reviewed economic contract, Sybil/fraud resistance, measurable service-quality criteria, anti-double-claim protection and reconciliation with the canonical ATC supply rules.
- AI agents may propose or prepare actions, but must not sign transactions, bypass wallet approval, control consensus, or authorize state changes solely from model output.

# Required architecture boundaries / ownership

- `a-townchain`: canonical blockchain core, transaction processing, consensus and settlement.
- `a-townchain/components/vm`: canonical ATC-VM.
- `atc-standards`: normative cross-project protocol, API/ABI, wallet/payment and compatibility contracts.
- `a-townchain-ecosystem`: architecture, ownership/dependency maps, integration contracts, reconciliation and evidence coordination only.
- Wallet, SDK, node-service, indexer, marketplace and payment implementations must be assigned to existing active canonical repositories after source-tree inventory; do not create a second SSOT.
- Aurora AI remains an orchestration/agent layer without consensus authority or direct deterministic state authority.
- Do not claim ERC/EVM, BSC, Solana, IBC, WalletConnect, Chainlink or third-party compatibility until the relevant adapter/protocol is implemented and conformance-tested.

# Security and reliability requirements

- Transaction signing must use the canonical transaction format, domain separation, signature policy and authorization contract.
- Protect against phishing, malicious RPC responses, stale/reorged data, replay, duplicate payment settlement, API abuse, key leakage and supply/accounting inconsistencies.
- RPC and indexer outputs must be treated as untrusted observations unless verified against canonical node data/proofs.
- Define finality and confirmation semantics before displaying a payment as settled.
- Cross-chain transfers require a separate bridge threat model and proof/finality policy; no mint/unlock from unauthenticated messages.
- Define privacy/data minimization, telemetry opt-in, retention, incident response, key rotation, vulnerability disclosure and service deprecation policy.
- Fail closed when authorization, finality, contract version, accounting or verification evidence is missing or contradictory.

# Delivery plan

1. Inventory existing active repositories, source trees, APIs, functions, tests and current wallet/RPC/indexer/payment implementations at exact 40-character commit SHAs.
2. Map each capability to a canonical owner; classify each source candidate as MAPPED, EXCLUDED (with reason), UNRESOLVED or BLOCKED.
3. Publish service-boundary diagram, trust-boundary/threat model, data flows and dependency matrix.
4. Register versioned contracts in `atc-standards`: RPC/API, wallet signing, payment request/settlement, indexer events/finality, service discovery and error semantics as applicable.
5. Build a minimum decentralized baseline: independent node operation, wallet-to-node connection configuration, verified transaction submission/status, and reproducible developer SDK examples.
6. Add conformance, adversarial, reorg/finality, duplicate/replay, outage/recovery and cross-repository integration tests.
7. Define optional service marketplace/reward mechanisms only after service-quality measurement and economic review.
8. Keep implementation PRs Draft until required gates and exact-HEAD evidence pass.

# Evidence and status contract

For each claim record repository, branch/ref, exact commit SHA, path/symbol/contract, workflow run → job → step → exit code/log/artifact. Distinguish SPECIFIED, IMPLEMENTED, TESTED, CI_VERIFIED, INTEGRATED and E2E_VERIFIED. Pending, skipped, missing, schema-only or stale results do not count as success.

# Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every proposed service has a canonical owner or an explicit BLOCKED decision.
- [ ] No duplicate SSOT or unapproved implementation is introduced.
- [ ] End-user and developer flows are documented with trust boundaries and failure behavior.
- [ ] Wallet signing and payment finality are grounded in normative contracts.
- [ ] RPC/indexer decentralization, provider choice, provenance and fallback behavior are specified.
- [ ] Compatibility claims are backed by adapter-specific conformance tests.
- [ ] Rewards/economics are separately specified; no unapproved issuance or reward percentages.
- [ ] Source-to-catalog reconciliation covers components, public functions, endpoints, events, CLI, tests and contracts.
- [ ] Security, integration and exact-HEAD evidence gates are terminal and reproducible.
- [ ] No automatic merge; no CI/security-gate weakening.

# Initial status

PROPOSED — NOT IMPLEMENTED — NOT VERIFIED.
